title: Feelings wheel and scenarios
subject: PSHE

intro: Lesson 3: Naming feelings. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

model.title: Your camera froze while presenting and others laughed.

parts.text: Notice: hot face, want to leave
Respond: breathe, rejoin, tell the teacher afterwards

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Embarrassed and hurt; breathe, rejoin, talk to the teacher

questions.q: Your best friend saves a place for someone else at the masjid study circle.
questions.a: Precise feeling: left out or jealous. Healthy response: tell your friend calmly how you felt, or sit with someone new.

questions.q: You have practised Surat Al-Mulk all week and the recitation test is tomorrow.
questions.a: Nervous or anxious. Response: one more calm practice, slow breathing, du'a, early sleep.

questions.q: A classmate presents your idea as theirs in a group task.
questions.a: Frustrated or resentful. Response: speak to them privately, or tell the teacher, without shouting.

questions.q: You forgot your homework for the second week running.
questions.a: Disappointed in yourself or guilty. Response: own it, apologise, plan a reminder.

questions.q: Your grandmother is ill in hospital abroad.
questions.a: Worried or helpless. Response: make du'a, call her if you can, talk to a parent about how you feel.

questions.q: You finish a project you found very hard.
questions.a: Proud or relieved. Response: say alhamdulillah, notice what helped, rest.

keywords.def: a feeling such as joy, anger or fear
the words we use to name feelings precisely
something that sets off a feeling
what we choose to do about a feeling

questions.q: Give a precise word: 'I worked hard but got a low mark.'
Where might you feel anxiety in your body?
Core: Feelings scenarios (pupil PDF): for six situations, name the precise feeling and one healthy response.
questions.a: Precise words and sensible responses for each.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, describe a mixed feeling you have had. Start: 'I felt both... and...'
questions.a: For example: I felt both excited and nervous on my first day at TGA.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why naming a feeling helps us control what we do.
questions.a: Naming slows us down and gives us a choice of response instead of reacting.

questions.q: Most precise word for 'I didn't get picked and I'm alone at break'?
questions.a: B) Lonely. Lonely names the feeling precisely; 'bad' and 'fine' hide it.

questions.q: Naming a feeling helps us... A) ignore it B) choose a healthy response C) blame others
Big question: what precise feelings could 'bad' hide? Name three.
